overall: The AG found the Medfield School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to identify the non-union personnel (the Superintendent) in the February 11 and March 11 notices and executive session announcements, but found the March 11 'Superintendent's Contract' topic sufficiently detailed, declined to find intent, and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: February 11 meeting notice did not identify the non-union personnel (the Superintendent) who would be discussed in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee does not dispute that its February 11 meeting notice should have identified the Superintendent as the non-union personnel under discussion during the executive session.

allegations.summary: Chair's announcement before the February 11 executive session did not identify the Superintendent as the non-union personnel to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, the Committee admits that the Chair’s announcement before entering executive session failed to specify that the Committee planned to discuss the Superintendent under the “non-union personnel” portion of the executive session.

allegations.summary: March 11 meeting notice repeated the generic executive session topic and did not identify the non-union personnel to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: The March 11 meeting notice listed the exact same executive session topic as the February 11 meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Chair's announcement before the March 11 executive session did not identify the Superintendent as the non-union personnel to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee also does not dispute that the March 11 announcement prior to entering should have specified that the Superintendent was the non-union personnel under discussion during the executive session.

allegations.summary: The open-session topic 'Superintendent's Contract' on the March 11 notice was allegedly not detailed enough (complainant wanted 'Contract Extension').
allegations.key_passage: We disagree and find that where the notice informed the public that the Board would be discussing the Superintendent’s contract, and that is in fact what it discussed, the notice was sufficient to comply with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the violations were intentional; the AG was asked to find intent under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c).
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to find an intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Allegations about the Committee's January 7 meeting were raised but were untimely under the 30-day complaint filing requirement.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review these allegations as they are untimely as complaints alleging violations of the Open Meeting Law must be filed with the public body within 30 days of the alleged violation

allegations.summary: Additional allegations raised in the request for further review that were not in the original complaint were not reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: In addition, we decline to review any additional allegations contained in the request for further review that were not included in the original complaints filed with the public body.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
